criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies overbroad MAE carve-outs for environmental industry/regulations
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the environmental-services-industry and Environmental Laws carve-outs as overbroad because they lack disproportionate-impact qualifiers, and proposes adding such qualifiers to both carve-outs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Proposes adding disproportionate impact qualifier to MAE carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly adds disproportionate-impact exceptions to both the environmental-services-industry carve-out and the Environmental Laws/regulatory carve-out, using the required formulation that the changes disproportionately affect the Company relative to other industry participants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Provides actual revised contract language for MAE definition
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes a full proposed replacement MAE definition with actual contract language, expressly adding disproportionate-impact exceptions to both the environmental-services-industry and Environmental Laws carve-outs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Explains rationale — environmental company needs MAE protection
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly explains that the unqualified industry and Environmental Laws carve-outs remove from the MAE analysis the two categories most likely to affect this environmental-services target—industry economics and environmental regulation—and therefore recommends disproportionate-impact qualifiers for both.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies missing interim covenant restricting affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that Section 6.01(b) lacks an interim restriction on transactions with Seller or Seller affiliates and proposes a consent requirement covering entry into, amendment, extension, renewal, termination, waiver, or modification of such affiliate transactions between signing and closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes covenant requiring Buyer consent for affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 6.01(b)(xiv), which prohibits the Company from entering into, amending, modifying, extending, renewing, or terminating any agreement or transaction with Seller or any Seller affiliate without Buyer's prior written consent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: References the above-market rent to Seller affiliate as rationale
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly ties the affiliate transaction restriction to the affiliate lease, stating that the Company pays $1,600,000 in annual rent to a Seller affiliate and that the interim covenant must prevent changes to such arrangements without Buyer consent.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies indemnification cap discrepancy (20% vs. 12.5%)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the Seller draft’s $43,000,000 cap as 20% of the $215,000,000 base enterprise value and contrasts it with the binding term sheet’s 12.5% cap of $26,875,000, proposing the required correction.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Proposes redline reducing cap to 12.5% / $26,875,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes replacing the $43,000,000 / 20% indemnification cap with $26,875,000, equal to 12.5% of the $215,000,000 base enterprise value, in both the executive summary and the proposed redline to Sections 1.01 and 9.04(b).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: References the term sheet as basis for cap correction
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the $43 million cap deviates from the binding term sheet and that the term sheet fixes the general cap at 12.5% of the $215 million Base Enterprise Value ($26.875 million). It cites Term Sheet § 8 and identifies the executed term sheet as dated September 10, 2025 in the materials reviewed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies that environmental reps survival period is too short
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the Seller's 12-month blanket survival period as inadequate for environmental representations, including Section 4.15 environmental compliance and permit matters, and proposes a 36-month survival period while reserving a longer limitations-period position.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Proposes extending environmental reps survival to at least 36 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes that the Environmental Representations survive for 36 months after closing in revised Section 9.01(c), and also reserves the option to seek survival through the full applicable statute of limitations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: References CERCLA/Dalton Creek exposure as rationale for longer survival
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly connects the requested longer survival period for environmental representations to the Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure and the ongoing Hargrove remediation project, noting that these liabilities may develop over several years.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies anti-sandbagging provision in Section 9.06
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 9.06 as an anti-sandbagging provision and quotes the language barring Buyer from indemnification for breaches or inaccuracies of which Buyer or its representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Proposes replacing with pro-sandbagging language
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces Section 9.06’s anti-sandbagging provision with pro-sandbagging language stating that Buyer’s indemnification and other remedies are not affected, limited, diminished, or impaired by any investigation or knowledge acquired before or after signing or Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Provides actual pro-sandbagging contract text
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes actual proposed pro-sandbagging contract language in the replacement for Section 9.06, stating that Buyer's indemnification and other remedies are not affected by investigations or knowledge acquired before or after signing or Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies need for Special Indemnity for Dalton Creek CERCLA matter
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes a separate Dalton Creek Special Indemnity in new Section 9.09, stating that the known EPA/CERCLA exposure should not be treated solely as a general environmental representation claim and should be outside the general basket and cap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity survival of 72 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in proposed Section 9.09(c) that the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity will survive the Closing for seventy-two (72) months, with claims permitted through that date.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity not subject to basket or cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in proposed Section 9.09(d) that the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity is not subject to the Basket Amount or the general Indemnification Cap. It also separately carves Special Indemnities out of the basket in Section 9.04(a) and the general cap in Section 9.04(b).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: References Dalton Creek liability range ($1.5M-$6M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites Dalton Creek's estimated potential liability range of $1,500,000 to $6,000,000 in both Schedule 9.09 and the rationale supporting the proposed Special Indemnity.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies problematic earnout operational covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 2.05(d) as problematic because it requires Buyer to operate consistently with past practice and in good faith to maximize the earnout. It recommends deleting those affirmative operational restrictions and replacing them with a narrow primary-purpose covenant.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Proposes limiting earnout covenant to no-frustration standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the seller’s affirmative past-practice and earnout-maximization obligations with a narrow covenant prohibiting actions taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the earnout payment, while preserving Buyer’s operational discretion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Explains rationale — Buyer integration/restructuring flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly explains that the seller’s broad earnout covenant would restrict Buyer’s platform integration and restructuring plans and create litigation risk over ordinary post-closing business decisions. It also states that the replacement preserves Buyer’s operational flexibility to integrate, restructure, consolidate, and make strategic changes.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies missing payoff letter requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that Section 2.03(d) permits repayment “at or promptly following the Closing” and that the Seller’s closing deliverables do not require payoff letters. It then proposes requiring executed payoff letters from each holder of Closing Indebtedness at least three business days before Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letters at least 3 business days pre-closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly requires executed payoff letters at least three Business Days before Closing. It also requires each payoff letter to include wire instructions and provides for delivery of lien-release documents, including UCC termination statements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes simultaneous repayment at closing through funds flow
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the “at or promptly following” mechanic with repayment of all Closing Indebtedness simultaneously at Closing through the agreed funds flow, and adds a corresponding closing condition.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letter delivery as a condition to closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes a new Section 7.02(h) making Seller's delivery of payoff letters and related lien-release documentation a condition to Buyer's obligation to close.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies missing government contract anti-assignment/novation requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft lacks specific government-contract anti-assignment, novation, and recognition provisions. It discusses the Anti-Assignment Act and FAR Part 42.12, names the Oregon DEQ, Washington Ecology, Army Corps of Engineers, and BLM contracts, and proposes related representations, covenants, and closing conditions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References specific government contracts requiring novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum specifically identifies the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Contract No. W912DR-21-D-0045 and Bureau of Land Management Contract No. L23PX-00412 as requiring novation or recognition packages. It also addresses corresponding approval or notification requests for the Oregon DEQ and Washington Ecology contracts.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Proposes closing condition or covenant for government contract novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes new Section 6.12 requiring Seller and the Company to notify contracting officers, prepare and submit federal and state novation/recognition packages, and use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain the required agreements before Closing. It also proposes a related closing condition in Section 7.02(i).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References Anti-Assignment Act or FAR provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, and FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12 as the legal basis for government-contract novation, recognition, and related notice requirements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies missing environmental permit transfer/notification covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller’s draft lacks a covenant addressing change-of-control notifications, approvals, transfers, or reissuance of the 23 environmental permits. It proposes new Section 6.13 requiring pre-closing submissions and post-closing cooperation for permit transfer, reissuance, amendment, notification, and approval processes.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Proposes cooperation covenant for environmental permit transfers
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 6.13, requiring Seller to assist both before and after closing with environmental permit notifications, applications, transfers, re-issuances, amendments, approvals, agency inquiries, and related documentation under applicable state requirements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Notes that permits may require notification even in a stock deal
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in the environmental permit covenant commentary that “A stock transaction does not eliminate change-of-control requirements” and discusses required notifications, consents, approvals, transfers, or reissuance for permits in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies missing R&W Insurance subrogation waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in Section 19 that the Seller's draft contains no provision addressing Buyer's R&W Insurance policy or the insurer's subrogation rights, and it proposes a fraud-only subrogation waiver.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Proposes subrogation waiver provision with fraud exception
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 10.13 requiring the R&W Insurance Policy to waive the insurer’s subrogation and recovery rights against Seller and related parties, expressly excepting claims arising from or relating to Seller fraud. It also identifies Granite Ridge Underwriters as the expected insurer.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: References R&W Insurance policy / Granite Ridge Underwriters
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that Buyer expects to obtain buy-side R&W Insurance from Granite Ridge Underwriters and connects that policy to a required insurer subrogation waiver, except for Seller fraud.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (duration)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft imposes a five-year non-compete and states that this exceeds the binding term sheet. It proposes replacing it with a three-year non-compete to conform to the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (geographic)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the Seller draft's five-year nationwide prohibition as exceeding the term sheet and replaces the geographic scope with Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (activity)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller’s draft imposes a five-year nationwide prohibition on “any business,” states that this exceeds the term sheet, and proposes limiting the activity scope to environmental remediation services and hazardous waste management services.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete duration to 3 years
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly narrows the non-compete period from five years to three years following the Closing Date, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete geographic scope to OR, WA, CA, NV
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) limits the non-compete to the States of Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete activity scope to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) narrows the non-compete from engaging in “any business” nationwide to businesses providing environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, expressly matching the required activity scope.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Notes enforceability risk of overbroad non-compete
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the five-year nationwide prohibition on “any business” would sweep in Seller’s legitimate construction and timber operations, and the proposed replacement carves out those existing operations. This satisfies the criterion even though it does not separately analyze enforceability.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification cap issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: The 20% versus 12.5% general indemnification cap discrepancy is expressly rated “High” priority in both the executive summary and Section 14, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Anti-sandbagging issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.06 (anti-sandbagging) is expressly assigned a priority of Critical, which is the highest tier and satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies provisions acceptable as drafted
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes a dedicated “Provisions to Leave Unchanged” section identifying multiple acceptable provisions and briefly explaining why they conform to the playbook or term sheet, including the basket amount and structure, knowledge definition, good-standing certificates, Delaware governing law, escrow amount, and purchase price/NWC mechanics.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum flags items for partner/client discussion
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly flags multiple issues for further partner/client discussion, including the government-contract novation closing condition, environmental-representation survival period, Dalton Creek factual inconsistencies and indemnity sub-cap, and permit-condition strategy. It also identifies Whitmore Capital/Marcus Devereaux and partner/client confirmation before finalizing positions.

criteria_results.title: Escrow amount correctly stated as $16,125,000 (7.5% of EV)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum consistently states the escrow amount as $16,125,000 and expressly identifies it as 7.5% of the $215,000,000 Base Enterprise Value, which is mathematically correct.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Proposes 36-month escrow holdback for Special Indemnity
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly provides a 36-month post-closing escrow holdback for Special Indemnities, distinct from the 18-month release for general indemnification claims. It specifically applies this 36-month holdback to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity in Sections 9.04(e), 9.09(e), and the proposed Escrow Agreement terms.

criteria_results.title: Earnout maximum correctly referenced as $25,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in the earnout discussion that the term sheet requires a "$25,000,000 maximum," so the maximum earnout payment is correctly referenced.

criteria_results.title: Earnout Adjusted EBITDA threshold correctly referenced as $38,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in the earnout discussion that the term sheet requires a $38,000,000 full-payment Adjusted EBITDA threshold. The threshold is correctly referenced and not materially misstated.

criteria_results.title: Earnout floor correctly referenced as $32,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the earnout has a $32,000,000 floor and uses linear interpolation between that floor and the $38,000,000 full-payment threshold, satisfying the required pro-rata structure.

criteria_results.title: References playbook as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the Buyer's M&A Playbook as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including the MAE qualifiers, earnout covenant, debt payoff mechanics, government-contract protections, environmental permits, indemnification cap/survival, anti-sandbagging, Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, and R&W insurance.

criteria_results.title: References term sheet as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the executed term sheet as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including the 12.5% indemnification cap, earnout operating covenant and timing, debt payoff letters, restrictive covenants, survival periods, escrow mechanics, Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, and R&W insurance subrogation waiver.

criteria_results.title: References environmental DD memo for at least one markup position
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum repeatedly cites the Environmental Due Diligence Summary / DD Memo as support for markup positions, including the Dalton Creek special indemnity, environmental representation survival, permit-transfer covenants, and government-contract protections.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies specific SPA section numbers for issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum ties well over 8 issues to specific SPA section numbers, including Sections 2.05, 2.03, 2.08, 4.15, 4.16, 4.17, 6.01, 6.09, 6.12, 6.13, 7.02, 9.01, 9.04, 9.06, 9.09, and 10.13.

criteria_results.title: Proposed redline language is actual contract text for at least 8 issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum provides insertion-ready proposed contract text for well over 8 issues, including the MAE definition, earnout covenant and mechanics, debt payoff, government contract representations and covenants, environmental permits, affiliate transactions, restrictive covenants, closing conditions, indemnification cap and survival, anti-sandbagging, the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, and R&W insurance.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies all three sources of Target indebtedness
criteria_results.reasoning: The payoff-letter discussion expressly identifies all three indebtedness sources: Cascade Mutual Bank's senior term loan, Pacific Lease Corp.'s equipment financing, and Evergreen Holdings/Seller's subordinated seller note. It also references the $42.3 million illustrative Closing Indebtedness elsewhere.
